results.title: Proceedings of the 2nd International Workshop on Multi-Agent Systems using Generative Artificial INtelligence for Automated Software Engineering
results.abstract: Welcome from the ChairsWelcome to MAS-GAIN 2026, the 2nd International Workshop on Multi-Agent Systems using Generative Artificial INtelligence for Automated Software Engineering.Following the successful first edition of the workshop, MAS-GAIN 2026 continues to bring together researchers and practitioners interested in the convergence of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAIN), and Automated Software Engineering.This second edition was held in Munich, Germany, in conjunction with the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE 2026).MAS-GAIN 2026 focuses on the engineering and application of multi-agent systems enhanced by generative AI for supporting and automating software engineering activities.As software systems continue to grow in complexity and scale, multi-agent architectures offer established mechanisms for distributed intelligence, collaboration, and autonomous problem solving, while recent advances in generative AI, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), provide new capabilities for reasoning, generation, and interaction.Their convergence opens new opportunities for addressing software engineering challenges through collaborative problemsolving automated generation, intelligent validation, and continuous evolution of software artifacts.The primary goal of MAS-GAIN 2026 is to provide a forum for researchers and practitioners to exchange ideas, methodologies, empirical results, experiences, and emerging research directions concerning the integration of multi-agent systems and generative AI in software engineering.The workshop encourages discussion of both theoretical foundations and practical implementations, with the broader objective of advancing the state of the art in agent-based software automation and identifying the opportunities and challenges that will shape the next generation of intelligent and autonomous software engineering solutions.The scope of this second edition encompasses a broad range of topics, including architectures and orchestration mechanisms for multi-agent systems, code synthesis and system modeling, integration of heterogeneous models, human-agent collaboration, verification and validation of AI-generated software artifacts, integration with development environments and software engineering tools, software maintenance and evolution, resource-efficient and local deployment of agentic systems, as well as industrial applications and empirical evaluations.At the same time, the contributions to this edition reflect an increasing emphasis on the software engineering of agentic systems themselves.As generative agents become capable of performing increasingly complex and autonomous tasks, iii members for their time, expertise, and careful and constructive reviews.We also thank the ASE 2026 organizers and the broader ASE community for hosting the second edition of MAS-GAIN within the long-standing tradition of the IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering.We invite all participants to engage actively with the program, exchange ideas with colleagues, and continue these discussions beyond the workshop.Further information about MAS-GAIN 2026 is available on the official workshop website (https://masgain.github.io/masgain/masgain2026/). We hope that MAS-GAIN 2026 provides an inspiring scientific forum, fosters new collaborations, and contributes to the continued development of the community around multi-agent generative AI for automated software engineering.

results.title: A Survey on Agentic Security: Applications, Threats and Defenses
results.abstract: In this work we present the first holistic survey of the agentic security landscape, structuring the field around the fundamental pillars of Applications, Threats and Defenses. We provide a comprehensive taxonomy of 274 papers that covers red-teaming, blue-teaming and domain-specific applications, attack surfaces on agentic systems, defense techniques, and both offensive and defensive evaluation frameworks. For each pillar, we first discuss the literature around the taxonomy and then perform a quantitative analysis to understand the patterns across these works. For the applications, we show their security-lifecycle coverage map, compare between red-teaming and blue-teaming agents, and analyze the adversarial use of red-teaming applications. On the threat side, we analyze the entry points and agent-loop stages that attacks target, their specificity to the agentic setting, and the threat models they assume. On the defense side, we analyze the prevailing defense strategies, their cost and security trade-offs, and where in the agent lifecycle they are deployed. Finally, we provide a deatiled cross-cutting analysis, where we map which defenses cover which attack classes and chart trends in agent architecture, backbone model usage, and data modality coverage. Taken together, these findings give a researcher a structural understanding of how agentic capabilities, vulnerabilities, and countermeasures relate to one another, and to identify where the field is concentrated and where it is thin.

results.title: Enhancing Healthcare Cybersecurity with AI: Protecting Medical Data and Ensuring Patient Safety
results.abstract: Enhancing Healthcare Cybersecurity with AI: Protecting Medical Data and Ensuring Patient Safety offers a practical guide to safeguarding sensitive medical data in today’s digital healthcare landscape. Combining cutting-edge AI techniques with proven cloud security practices; this book explores strategies for building secure, compliant, and resilient healthcare systems. From protecting patient information under HIPAA and HITRUST regulations to implementing Zero Trust models and automation frameworks, readers will gain actionable insights to prevent breaches, ensure system reliability, and enhance patient safety. Ideal for security professionals, healthcare IT leaders, and anyone interested in the intersection of AI, cloud, and healthcare, this book bridges the gap between innovation and compliance.
